# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Non-generalizing / hardcoded answers | 110-2, 38332, 3911, 5192 (pure hardcode); plus [1,0,0]/[0,1,0] partial-pass tasks 39046, 51359, 30709, 56427, 11842, 353-29 that pass the visible case but fail the two hidden re-runs | Final code block is re-run on 2 hidden input files with DIFFERENT data (adapter.py:1194-1198), scoring is HARD (all 3 must pass). Agent writes constants/answers read off the visible file, so cases 2/3 fail. | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule about the grading/re-run contract) | Add re-run contract + "compute from data, never hardcode" |
| 2 | Dynamic-array / spill formulas don't recalc → blank | 47741 (TEXTJOIN+WORKDAY over `{10,12}` array), 11842 | Headless LibreOffice recalc leaves spill/array-function cells blank; agent wrote such a formula. Ordinary scalar formulas (SUMIF/COUNTIF/INDEX-MATCH/WORKDAY) DO recalc — passing tasks «redacted» rely on that. | KNOWLEDGE (recalc limitation) | Narrow formula guidance: ordinary funcs OK, avoid spill/array funcs; compute those in Python |
| 3 | Wrong output TYPE | 51958 (date written as text string), and any date-as-text cases | Grader `transform_value`/`compare_cell_value` (evaluation.py) compares by type then value; a date stored as text ≠ a real date cell (which normalizes to a float serial). | KNOWLEDGE / output-contract | State the type contract: numbers as numbers, dates/times as datetime objects |
| — | Genuine reasoning/logic errors | 325-44, 450-9, 50051, 50630, 55931, 56637, 56996, 57090, 57232, 59667, 59743, 53367, CF_11072, 73-45 | Task-specific logic/ambiguity; not a prompt knowledge gap | out of scope for prose | none (see skipped) |
| — | INFRASTRUCTURE | 73-45 (recalc FAILED per feedback) | formula recalc failed → stale values; adapter flags "not a prompt defect" | ENVIRONMENT | none |

## Changes made this iteration (all in prompt.md — the system prompt)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Add missing rule / output-contract (menu #4, #8) | prompt.md | New "HOW YOUR SOLUTION IS GRADED" block: final code is replayed on 2 hidden inputs, so compute every value from the data read at runtime; never hardcode a computed/data-dependent value or copy the instruction's example results. General rule across the whole task class. | Yes — all 24 passers already generalize (they pass all 3 cases); rule is additive, no passer hardcodes. Parenthetical exempts fixed labels the instruction dictates. |
| 2 | Add missing rule + WHY (menu #2, #4) | prompt.md | Formula guidance narrowed: ordinary scalar functions are fine (grader recalculates them); avoid dynamic-array/spill/array-constant functions (UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT/SEQUENCE/array TEXTJOIN/WORKDAY) which recalc blank — compute in Python. | Yes — passing formula tasks use only ordinary funcs (SUMIF/COUNTIF/INDEX-MATCH/WORKDAY/SUMPRODUCT); narrowing does not touch them. Still prefers Python values, so no literal-passer pushed to formulas. |
| 3 | Tighten output contract (menu #8) | prompt.md | Type contract: grader compares by type then value; write numbers as numbers, dates/times as real datetime/date/time objects, not text that looks like a date. | Yes — passing datetime tasks (41297, 59259) already write datetime objects; numeric-string still matches per transform_value, so nothing regresses. |
| 1-3 | Ordered pre-save checklist (structural lever) | prompt.md | 3-item "Before you save, confirm" checklist making compute-from-data + range restriction + type an unavoidable pre-finish step, not just advice. | Additive; restates existing constraints as a gate. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what changes)
- 38332 trace: final block `for row in range(2,6): ws.cell(...,4).value = 1` → constant, passes case 1 only. With EDIT 1 the grading contract makes clear the block is re-run on different data; agent would compute the count from column A per row instead of writing `1`, so cases 2/3 can match. Verified against adapter.py:1194-1198 (filename-swap replay) + hard scoring.
- 3911 / 5192 / 110-2 traces: emit a hardcoded results table / dict / inferred `array_1..3` sets. EDIT 1 explicitly forbids "hardcoded list/dict/table of results" and "values quoted in the wording" → forces computation from the input columns.
- 47741 trace: writes `=TEXTJOIN("-",,TEXT(WORKDAY(B4,{10,12},...)))` → spill/array formula → recalc blank → [0,0,0]. EDIT 2 names this exact construct as to-avoid and directs computing in Python. Confirmed passing task 58109 uses plain WORKDAY (scalar) and is explicitly kept OK.
- 51958 trace: writes `ws["B2"] = "09/08/21 10:06"` (string) for a value the answer stores as a date. Per evaluation.transform_value a str that can't float()-parse stays str while a datetime GT becomes a float serial → `type(v1)!=type(v2)` → mismatch. EDIT 3 directs writing a real datetime object → same-type comparison.

## Blast-radius per edit
- EDIT 1: BOUNDED/additive. Class = all tasks; new behavior (compute from data) is correct for EVERY task and is what all 24 passers already do. No passer relies on hardcoding.
- EDIT 2: BOUNDED/narrowing. Only changes behavior on spill/array-formula cases; ordinary-function passers (7 formula tasks) explicitly unaffected.
- EDIT 3: BOUNDED/additive clarification of the output contract passers already satisfy (numbers/datetimes). Numeric strings still pass via transform_value, so no numeric passer regresses.

## Process & features used
- Serial (no subagents): I read the adapter (re-run replay at adapter.py:1194-1198, hard scoring at score()) and the vendored evaluation.py (transform_value/compare_cell_value) directly to ground every rule in the real grader, then dumped all 26 failing + 24 passing final code blocks to cluster by root cause. Grounding in code, not guessing, was the priority.
- Prior iterations: none exist yet (first optimization iteration; prior_iterations/ empty, LEDGER has only baseline).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- Ordinary scalar formulas MUST stay allowed — 7 passing tasks depend on LibreOffice recalc of SUMIF/COUNTIF/INDEX-MATCH/WORKDAY/SUMPRODUCT. Do not add a blanket "no formulas" rule.
- Numeric strings match numbers (transform_value rounds float()-able strings) — don't over-tighten the type rule against them.
- The range-restriction rules (write only within answer_position) — several passers depend on not touching neighbor cells.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- Genuine logic/reasoning errors (325-44, 450-9, 50051, 50630, 55931, 56637, 56996, 57090, 57232, 59667, 59743, 53367, CF_11072, 73-45): the agent's approach is wrong for the task's semantics, not a knowledge gap the prompt can state generally. Adding task-specific hints would overfit and fail the held-out gate. Several will still benefit indirectly from EDIT 1/2/3 (generalization, formula, type) but I did not hand-code their logic.
- 73-45: adapter feedback marks recalculation FAILED (infrastructure) — not a prompt defect; left untouched.
